title: Hong Kong Finance Chief Says Public Tokenized Funds Grew Sevenfold in a Year
description: At a November 16 regulatory forum, Financial Secretary Paul Chan reported sevenfold growth in publicly offered tokenized funds and described round-the-clock money-market fund trading.
why_it_matters: The government’s new growth statement signals broader distribution of regulated tokenized investment products, while its proposed licensing expansion underscores that operational adoption remains tied to investor protection and supervision.
keyTakeaways: Paul Chan reported approximately sevenfold annual growth in publicly offered tokenized funds, without publishing the underlying measurement series in his speech.
Two tokenized money market funds have traded around the clock on a licensed Hong Kong platform since October, according to Chan.
Hong Kong plans a bill before year-end extending digital-asset licensing to dealing, advice, management and custody.
body:
Hong Kong Financial Secretary Paul Chan said on November 16 that tokenized funds offered to the public in the city had grown roughly sevenfold over one year. Speaking at the Bloomberg Global Regulatory Forum 2026, Chan described tokenization as moving beyond pilots into routine financial use.

He also said two tokenized money market funds had been trading around the clock on a licensed platform since October. The speech did not provide the underlying starting and ending fund values or define the precise measure behind the sevenfold comparison, so the figure should be treated as an official statement rather than an independently reconstructed market series.

Chan outlined a further regulatory step: Hong Kong intends to introduce legislation before the end of 2026 extending licensing to digital-asset dealing, advisory, management and custody services. He emphasized applying conventional product requirements alongside safeguards for new risks. Separately, he said two of the first 36 stablecoin licence applicants had received licences in April and subsequently launched Hong Kong dollar stablecoins.
